summary: Returns the value after checking that it is not a number with a fractional part.
description: JavaScript has one numeric type, so `1.0` and `1` are the same value: the question answered is whether a fraction survives at runtime, not how the literal was written. The infinities have no fraction and are excluded.
`isX` and `nonX` answer a question and never interrupt control flow; `requireX` and `requireNonX` hand the value back or throw. The scheme is explained in [](validation-conventions.md).

params.message: The message of the exception. A default is used when omitted.
params.strict: When `true`, a string counts as empty only if it has no characters at all; by default whitespace is trimmed first.

returns: the same value, with a number with a fractional part excluded from its type.

throws.IllegalArgumentException: the value is a number with a fractional part.

examples.title: What passes and what does not
examples.body:
```javascript
requireNonFloat(42); // => 42
requireNonFloat(1.0); // => 1.0
requireNonFloat(1.5); // throws IllegalArgumentException
requireNonFloat(-0.1); // throws IllegalArgumentException
```
